name: Martine Rothblatt
sec_insider_companies: UNITED THERAPEUTICS Corp (UTHR) - Chairperson & CEO; BETA Technologies, Inc. (BETA) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Martine Rothblatt cofounded Sirius Satellite Radio in 1990 but left soon after the company's 1993 IPO.
Rothblatt moved into biotech after her daughter was diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension, a disease that was deadly at the time.
She founded United Therapeutics in 1996; it sells five FDA-approved drugs to help people with the disease.
The publicly-traded company is experimenting with pig cloning and genetic modification to create lung transplants the human body doesn't reject.
The company's pig 'pharm' in Blacksburg, Virginia is the world's largest cloner of pigs.
forbes_facts: Rothblatt is an activist for transgender rights. She and her wife Bina have been married for more than 30 years.
Rothblatt is working to develop the first electric helicopter.

name: Masateru Uno
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Masateru Uno is the founder and chairman of Cosmos Pharmaceutical, which has over 1,500 drugstores in Japan.
The company sells medicines and cosmetics as well as food and beverages.
Masateru's son, Yukitaka, is a director of the company and heads product development.
Cosmos Pharmaceutical trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

name: Thomas Eisert
forbes_bio: Thomas Eisert is a shareholder of Phoenix Contact Group, a family-owned German electrical engineering company.
Phoenix was founded by Hugo Knumann merchant who started a distribution business for electrical products following the first world war.
Knumann died in 1953, but not before hiring an electrical engineer, Josef Eisert, who along with Ursula Lampmann took over and transformed the business into a manufacturer.
Five members of the Eisert family, including Josef's son Klaus, remain shareholders in the company, which has annual sales of more than 3 billion euros.

name: Ivan Savvidis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Ivan Savvidis, a Greek-Russian businessman, is the founder of Agrocom Group, whose assets included Russian tobacco firm Donskoy Tabak.
Savvidis sold Donskoy Tabak for $1.6 billion to Japan Tabacco in March 2018.
Seen as a Putin ally, Savvidis is a former member of the Russian parliament.
Through his Greek company Dimera, he owns a stake in soccer team FC PAOK in Thessaloniki, Greece, where he also operates a port.
He got his start as a worker at the Don State Tobacco Factory (now Donskoy Tabak) and was elected general director in 1993.
forbes_facts: In 2022 Savvidis bid for the port of Alexandroupoli in northeastern Greece but in the long run the Greek government decided not to sell it.

name: Kishin RK
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2024)
forbes_bio: Kishin RK is among Singapore's leading developers with his Royal Holdings/RB Capital property empire, which he owns and runs together with his father Raj Kumar.
He's been on a dealmaking spree after a 2011 family settlement between his father and uncle Asok Kumar Hiranandani, who's also a billionaire.
Prize holdings include the 442-room Holiday Inn Express at Clarke Quay, Holiday Inn Little India  and the hotel Intercontinental Singapore Robertson Quay.
He bought the Porcelain Hotel in Singapore's Chinatown, which was refurbished and reopened in 2023 as the 134-room Hotel 1900.
In 2025, they set up their RB Family Office in Abu Dhabi to tap investment opportunities in the Middle East.
forbes_facts: Kishin's RB Food Group owns a portfolio of brands, such as members' club 1880, cocktail bar Employees Only, Roia restaurant and cloud kitchen company TiffinLabs.
The name RB is derived from the erstwhile Royal Brothers, a 77-year-old property group with roots in textile trading.

name: Antonio Gallardo Ballart
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2022); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Antonio Gallardo Ballart's father founded pharmaceutical company Almirall in 1943 in Barcelona.
When their father died in 1988, Antonio and his brother Jorge took over running Almirall.
The company listed its shares in Madrid in 2007; Antonio and his brother Jorge control the company.
Antonio Gallardo Ballart served as vice president and advisor until 2014, when he retired.
Members of the third generation of the Gallardo family now work at the company.

name: Chen Kaichen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Kaixuan is vice chairman of Guangzhou-headquartered Liby Group, a supplier of washing detergents and soap.
Chen co-founded Liby in 1994 with his brother Chen Kaixuan, who is also a billionaire.
His daughter Danxia chairs Cheerwin Group, a Hong Kong-listed consumer and pet products company invested by Chen Kaixuan.

name: Prateek Boob
forbes_bio: Prateek Boob cofounded  edtech company Physicswallah as an e-learning app in 2020, together with Alakh Pandey.
Physicswallah started with prep courses for the entrance test to the Indian Institute of Technology as well as for medical college entrance exams.
It now provides learning modules for students from grades one to 12.
The cofounders became billionaires after taking the company public in November 2025.
forbes_facts: Physicswallah also offers offline coaching through its network of Vidyapeeth centers.
Boob has a B.Tech degree in mechanical engineering from IIT (Benaras Hindu University).

name: Alexander Rakshin
forbes_bio: Alexander Rakshin is the founder and owner of Maria-Ra, a Russian retail chain.
He founded his first Maria-Ra store in 1993 in Barnaul and has built the business into Siberia's largest retail chain with more than 1,300 locations.
Rakshin has 25% in the most operational companies. His family members (wife, son and daughter) own the same stakes.
The family also invests in commercial real estate, including shopping malls and markets, as well as office buildings in Siberia, Moscow and Saint Petersburg.
Rakshin got his start in business in 1990 when he and his partners established fur farm with silver foxes and minks to produce fur hats. He left the venture to start Maria-Ra three years later.
forbes_facts: Rashkin finished won second-place in the 1973 USSR junior in cross-country skiing championship and worked as physical education teacher in Barnaul, Siberia.
His retail business is named after his mother, Maria Rakshina.

name: Joseph Nahmad
forbes_bio: Joseph Nahmad is one of three sons of the late art billionaire Ezra Nahmad, who died in 2023.
Ezra Nahmad, along with his billionaire brother David, was an international megadealer of modern and impressionist art.
At the time of his death, the brother' art inventory, which is stored in a duty-free warehouse in Geneva, Switzerland, was worth almost $7 billion.
Ezra's half of the collection - which includes works by more than 30 blue chip artists, from Monet and Matisse to Renoir and Rothko - was split evenly among his three sons after his death.
The family also owns 300 Picassos worth at least $1 billion and real estate in London, Monaco and the U.S.

name: Xiang Wenbo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Xiang Wenbo is chairman of Sany Group, a heavy equipment manufacturer.
Xiang is one of three billionaires from Sany Group, along with Liang Wengen and Mao Zhongwu.
Xiang is a graduate of Dalian University of Technology with a master's degree in molding.

name: Tan Lili
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Tan Lili's fortune stems from his stake in Haid Group, a supplier of aquatic products and livestock feed.
Haid is headquartered in Guangzhou, China.
Haid went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2009.

name: Randolph Lerner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Randy Lerner owes his riches to his billionaire dad, Al Lerner (d. 2002), who made a fortune in credit cards.
His father got his start as a furniture salesman then invested in Cleveland-area real estate. He later bought control of Equitable Bancorp in 1981.
Equitable Bancorp merged with Maryland National to form credit card giant MBNA, which was acquired by Bank of America for $35 billion in 2005.
forbes_facts: The Lerners bought the Cleveland Browns in 1999, bringing pro football back to the city. They sold the team to billionaire Jimmy Haslam for about $1 billion in 2012.
Lerner and his family sold the English football club Aston Villa for $88 million to Chinese businessman Tony Xia in 2016 after a decade of ownership.
